build: Palace Software disk, 1987, two sides (C64 Preservation Project G64s, barbarian_s1[palace_1987](!) and barbarian_s2[palace_1987](!), SHA-256 1db548f7... and 204d8daf...)

exclude: zero page: the processor port and the game's variables, set at run time

the sound driver's variables, the eight sprite slots, the mirror and mask tables (built at the start), the cell stashes (filled at the start) and the compose buffer, all written at run time; at the hand-over the loader is still there
the place of fighter block 0: block number 0 means none, so these 63 zero bytes are never read
the sprite pointers after the screen, written every frame by sprite_registers
the arena buffer, the strip's clean copy and the backdrop swap's buffer: zeros in the load, written at run time, with two runs of 32 zero bytes between them that nothing uses
the end of the table file loaded at $CB00: 116 bytes of $FF that nothing reads
bytes the file loaded at $E000 carries between the music and the scene shapes: $00 and $FF in turn, the pattern of memory nothing wrote, never read

the same pattern at the end of that file, to $FFEF, except $FFD0-$FFEF: 6502 code and then Z80 code, each writing the Commodore 128's MMU registers ($FF00 and $D505) to change processors, which no instruction of the game reaches (likely left in the file by a C128 used to save it); then the hardware vectors, which the game writes at the start

The cartridge signature the KERNAL looks for at $8000 on a reset: the cold-start vector, the warm-start vector (the one RESTORE takes) and the bytes $C3 $C2 $CD $38 $30, "CBM80" in PETSCII. Both vectors point to start ($8009), so a reset or RESTORE restarts the game instead of BASIC. The loader's last instruction, jmp ($8000), also starts the game through the first vector.
The game's entry, from the loader's jmp ($8000) or a reset. Turns interrupts off and sets sound_mode ($B8) to 0, the sound effects (the tune off), then falls into restart.

The common start and the target of the Q key's restart (restart_game, $94D2): sets the game's variables (init_vars), the processor port ($00 = $2F, $01 = $25: the I/O chips in, BASIC and the KERNAL out), the video chip's bank 1 ($4000-$7FFF) through CIA 2, the hardware IRQ vector to irq ($9511) and the NMI vector to nmi ($9542). Then the video chip: multicolour bitmap ($D011 = $3B, $D016 = $18), the screen at $4400 and the bitmap at $6000 ($D018 = $18), sprite multicolours black and light red, and a raster interrupt at line $FA. Clears the sprites, saves the arena strip, colours the panel, resets the sprite slots and both fighters, and builds the mirror and mask tables. With the tune off (sound_mode positive) it stops CIA 2's timers, turns every CIA interrupt off, then starts CIA 1's timer A (latch $2710, the sound's effects) and timer B (latch $5161, the sound's sequencer) with their interrupts on, silences the sound and fades the volume in. A restart with the tune playing leaves the timers and the sound as they are. Then it enables interrupts and runs main_loop.

The game's loop, one pass at a time, about five passes a second in play: the panel's animations, the panel's label, the middle number and the strength display, the two-player timeout, the players' sticks, the computer's moves, the arena redrawn from its clean copy, each fighter's next frame, the poses, the decapitation, the goblin, the sprite overlays, the arena copied to the screen, the distance, the hits, the sprite shapes mirrored when asked, the end of a roll past (end_roll_past), the walk-on that starts a bout (walk_on), the walk-off that ends one (walk_off), the idle fighters, the keyboard, and last Drax's throws (drax_throws) and the ending's sprites (scene_sprites), which do nothing outside the ending. Never returns: the jmp at $8103 closes the loop.
Clears the eight sprite slots the interrupt moves and animates (motion script, picture sequence, direction, speeds and their counters) and sets each sequence's read index to 2, its first entry.

Puts both fighters back at the start of a bout: frame 0 of no next move, the start column from fighter_start_x ($7F42), the move $80 (standing), facing as their number (player 1, number 0, faces right; number 1 faces left), the panel animation and full strength (reset_strength), and the score shown as 00000 (reset_score_text). Leaves bout_state ($B4) at $FF, the walk-on.
For fighter X, with A = the panel animation to run: starts that animation at its first entry (bit 7 set in anim_script, $5B), sets the strength to 12 ($93) and the idle counter ($95) to $FF.
Writes "00000" over fighter X's score in its panel message (message $87 or $88, characters 3 to 7).

Fills mirror_table ($02AA-$03A9) with each byte value's mirror image as a multicolour pixel row: the four two-bit pixels in the opposite order. The fighters facing left and the mirrored sprite shapes are drawn through it.

Fills mask_table ($03AA-$04A9): for each byte of fighter graphics, a mask with %11 where a two-bit pixel is 00 (see-through) and %00 where it is drawn. draw_fighter ANDs the background with it before ORing in the fighter.
Steps the snake animations at the top of the side pillars, one picture each pass: for each fighter (1, then 0) whose anim_script ($5B,x) has bit 7 set, runs anim_step.

One step of fighter X's snake animation. The script is snake_scripts[$5B,x AND $7F] ($BC98): a header of column, row, width and height in cells, then two-byte entries from offset 4. anim_pos ($5D,x) is the offset of the entry to read. An entry of 4 or more is the address of a picture, copied into the bitmap (anim_draw) at the header's place, and the offset moves on by 2: one picture a pass. An entry below 4 is a command: 0 starts the script again, 1 jumps to the offset in the byte after it (plus 4), 2 starts the script numbered in the byte after it and runs its first step at once, 3 stops (bit 7 of $5B,x cleared, the last picture stays).

Copies a picture of $AB cells by $AC cells into the bitmap: from (pointer $75) eight bytes a cell, a row of cells at a time, to (pointer $77), the next row of the bitmap 320 bytes on. The pictures are kept in the bitmap's own order, a cell's eight bytes after another's.
Prints the label under the arena: DEMO (message $84) while the demo plays, else 1PLR or 2PLR (message $82 plus players, $BD).
Prints the two digits between the scores (message $86): in a two-player game the clock ($C8) in seconds, else a 0 and the skill level ($BE), so a one-player game shows 00 to 07.

Prints both strength displays and both scores. For each fighter the strength (0 to 12, $93,x) picks one of the messages $8B-$97, two rows of six half circles; the column (0 for player 1, 34 for player 2, from strength_columns at $BC91) is written into both of its records before it is printed. Then prints the fighter's score, message $87 or $88.

The end of a two-player fight on time. When the clock ($C8) has run out in a two-player game, outside the demo and with no fighter rolled past the other ($B2 positive), it sets walking_back ($B5) and walks each fighter back (move $82) to its mark (walk_back_x, $7F44, by facing), standing it there (move $80). When both stand, it clears walking_back, restores both strengths and snakes, sets bout_state ($B4) to $80 for a new walk-on and changes the backdrop (swap_backdrop).

The start of each bout. While bout_state ($B4) is negative, outside the select mode, both fighters walk forward (move $81) until they are less than 6 columns apart; the first pass pays any time bonus still owed (time_bonus), resets the clock and starts the walk-on tune ($89-$8B on the three voices) unless voice 1 is busy. Once they are close it sets bout_state to 0, the fight, sets both idle counters ($95, $96) to $FF and, with the tune off, fades the sound out and back in for the effects.

In a two-player game, outside the demo, when a fighter has just won (winner, $B6, negative), counts the clock down to 0, adding 10 points (score_ten, $BC93) to the winner's score for each second left, printing the score and the clock at each step and waiting a frame between them (wait_ticks). Clears $B6.

After a death (dead, $AF, negative) and once the loser's body has been dragged off (its column 40 or more), turns the winner back to its usual facing if it faces the other way (move $9D; fighter 0 faces right, fighter 1 left), then walks it back to its mark (move $82, walk_back_x at $7F44). When it stands there, the bout is over: both fighters are reset at their start columns with full strength (scores reset too in the demo), bout_state goes to $FF for a walk-on, and bit 7 of the death, goblin and drag flags is cleared. When fighter 1 lost with its sprite shapes mirrored, it asks for them to be mirrored back (flip_request, $B7). Then: the demo changes backdrop; a one-player game the player lost waits 200 frames and restarts in the demo; a one-player game the player won goes up a skill level and changes the backdrop, or, after the win at level 7, starts the ending (start_ending). The two-player path, which pays the time bonus, never runs on this side.

The win at skill level 7, the eighth fight, ends the tournament. bout_state ($B4) is set to the backdrop's number, 0 or 1, so the walk-on that walk_off asked for does not start, and if the throne room (backdrop 0) is up swap_backdrop changes to the hall of arches, where Drax stands in the left-hand arch and Mariana in the right. A game won bout by bout is in the hall already: the backdrop changes with every win, and level 7 is the eighth bout. Then any mirroring of fighter 1's pieces still asked for is done (flip_sprite_shapes), scene_flag ($BB) is set, the fighters are drawn once (draw_fighters_once) and, 50 frames later, Drax leaves his arch (swap_cells_13) and the scene's sprite shapes come in (swap_shape_bank). From here the main loop's drax_throws and scene_sprites run the ending.

Drax's throws, once a main-loop pass while the ending runs (scene_flag, $BB, negative) and the barbarian has not reached him (scene_flag_2, $BC, positive). On a pass with scene_number ($CB) at 0 and no star in flight, Drax throws one from sprite 4: picture sequence $95, X 255 at the right with the ninth bit clear, Y $A2, and a motion script from star_motions picked by bit 0 of the raster line ($D012), $8A high or $8B low, the pick kept in star_kind ($CC); the throw's sound, $DD, goes to all three voices. scene_number goes to 1 with each throw and back to 0 on the next pass, and stays 0 while the star flies: scene_sprites shows Drax throwing for one pass and standing the rest of the time. Once the star's column (its X / 8, less 6) is left of the barbarian's, star_strikes decides whether it hits, and reach_drax whether he has got to Drax.

The star has reached the barbarian (fighter 0). If his move is one of the dodges for its kind (dodge_lists, by star_kind: a crouch, a leg chop or a roll under a high star, a jump over a low one), the star goes (star_dodged). Otherwise he falls dead (move $9B), the fighters are drawn until 150 frames have passed (draw_fighters_once), YOUR END HAS COME is printed (message $89), and 200 frames later the game restarts in the demo (restart_game).
Takes the dodged star away: sprite 4's picture sequence and motion script stop and the sprite is switched off.

Once the barbarian stands at column 28 or beyond, he has reached Drax: scene_flag_2 ($BC) is set, which ends the throws, and sprites 0 to 4 are switched off (stop_sprites), so Drax and his star vanish. The barbarian stands (move $80) for 25 frames, then walks back (move $82) to his mark, column 3 (walk_back_x), the fighters drawn every 5 frames. The walk-on tune plays ($89, $8A and $8B on the three voices) and, 50 frames later, Mariana leaves her arch (swap_cells_23) and stands in the arena as sprites (scene record 2, scene_sprites). The barbarian walks forward (move $81) to column 23 and raises his sword (move $93); 150 frames later THANKS BIG BOY is printed (message $8A), and 250 frames after that the game restarts in the demo (restart_game). Below column 28 it returns at once.
Starts the barbarian (fighter 0) on move $80 + A from its first frame: next_move = A, move = A + $80, frame index 0.

One frame of the fighters outside the main loop, for the ending's waits: the strip cleared (clear_strip), both fighters moved on and drawn (animate_fighters), their overlay sprites placed (place_overlays) and the strip shown (show_strip).

Waits A frames: sets wait_count ($CA), which the interrupt's work at line $FA (tick_counters, $9938) counts down, and loops until it is 0. A frame in which the interrupt's work is still busy from the last one does not count.
Switches off sprite slots 0 to 4 (sequence and motion cleared, their bits out of the sprite enable shadow $17). Used by restart_game.
Reads the sticks of the human players outside the demo: fighter 0 alone in a one-player game, both in a two-player game ($BD), through read_stick.

Turns fighter X's joystick into a move. Does nothing during a death, the walk-back on time, a roll past, the walk-on or the select mode, nor while the fighter is in one of the three moves listed at no_input_moves ($BDD3: $9B, the fall to death; $88, the headless body; $93). Reads the port (player 1 on port 2 through $DC00 with X = 0, player 2 on port 1 through $DC01), keeps the five switch bits as pressed-is-1, finds the direction in the stick list for the fighter's facing (stick_lists, $CE58), and passes it to stick_to_move.

Keeps the stick value in stick ($6D,x) and finds its direction (bits 0-3) in the nine-entry list at (pointer $81): Y = 0 none, 1 forward, 2 back, 3 down, 4 up, 5 down and forward, 6 up and forward, 7 down and back, 8 up and back (the lists swap left and right by facing).

Picks the row of moves the stick can lead to from fighter X's current move: move_rows_free ($CE6E) without fire, move_rows_fire ($CE8A) with fire, row k at move_rows + 9 * k ($CEA6). Leaves the row's address in pointer $87 and Y as the direction.

Starts the move the row gives for direction Y, unless the move under way still holds the stick (next_move, $6B,x, negative) or the row gives that same move, and leaves the taunt ($9A) alone while its direction would keep it. The new move goes in move ($67,x) with bit 7, the row's entry as it stands in next_move ($6B,x), and the frame index ($69,x) back to 0. Every entry but stand and the two walks has bit 7, so such a move holds the stick until its list reaches its command, where animate_fighter clears next_move.

For the human fighters, in play (not the demo, a death, the walk-on, the walk-back or the select mode): when a fighter's stick has been left alone until its idle counter ($95,x, counted down by the interrupt once a frame from $FF) reaches 0, it starts move $9A, frames $52, $53, $54, $53, $54, $53, $54 and back to standing; any stick input sets the counter back to $FF. A fighter in one of the moves at no_input_moves ($BDD3) is left alone.

The computer's fighters: both in the demo, fighter 1 in a one-player game, none in a two-player game; nothing during a roll past, a death, the walk-on, the select mode or the walk-back. For the fighter X it reads its opponent's pose ($6F) and the distance between them ($AA, distance_class $CA0E): ai_pose_rows ($CA36) gives the pose's row of eight, the distance class picks a list of eight stick values (ai_choices, $CB9C + 8 * n), and the skill level's 32-entry list (ai_level_picks, $C8FE) picks one of the eight, indexed by ai_counter ($CD AND $1F). In the demo the counter is taken from the low bytes of CIA 1's two timers; in a game it only goes up by one each call, so the computer works through its 32 entries in order. The stick value goes through the same find_stick, stick_row and stick_to_move as a player's, with the stick list for facing right.
A times 8 as a 16-bit number: low byte in A, high byte in $88.

Sets each fighter's pose ($6F,x), the frame it shows now: the entry of its move's frame list (move_frames, $BCDC) just before the frame index ($69,x), or the first when the index is 0. The hits and the computer read the pose.

Tests both fighters' blows (hit_test, fighter 1 then 0) unless a roll past, a death, the walk-on, the select mode, the walk-back on time or the flag at $BB is under way; after a blow that killed (dead, $AF, negative) it gives the winner its move (winner_move).

Whether fighter X's blow lands on the other fighter. Only some poses are blows: the twelve in attack_poses ($C31C), each with a list in hit_lists ($C328) of pairs (the victim's pose, a hit record) ending in $FF. When the victim's pose (below $5B) is in the list and the fighters are less than 8 columns apart, bit (distance) of the record's first byte says whether the blow reaches. When it does not, a later pair for the same pose is tried, but its record is not read from hit_records: hit_record_at builds the address's high byte in $88, which is cleared only once, before the loop ($87EE), so a second call starts from what the first left there and reads four bytes elsewhere in memory. The first record that reaches (hit_records, $C808, four bytes) then gives the victim's new move (0 for none), the sound and damage (hit_effect), and the blood and the points (hit_blood, hit_score). One blow a call, and none once a fighter is dead.
Y = the index of fighter X's pose in attack_poses ($C31C, twelve entries), or $FF when the pose is not a blow.
Sets pointer $87 to hit record n (the byte at (pointer $8B),Y): hit_records ($C808) plus four times n.

The record's third byte. Its high four bits pick a sound from hit_sounds ($C8A4, three bytes, a request for each voice, 0 for none), which goes into the three voices' requests ($DD-$DF) with interrupts off. A low four bits other than 0 make the blow hurt: the victim's snake starts its hit animation (script 2 or 3) if it is not already moving, and its strength ($93,x) goes down by one of its 12 points, whatever the value. At 0 the victim is dead: dead ($AF) gets its number with bit 7, and its move becomes $9B, the fall.

The record's fourth byte, high four bits: 0 for none, else a sprite from hit_sprites ($C8B3, three bytes: picture sequence, Y position, column offset) in the first free sprite slot of the eight (sequence $0292,x not negative), placed from the attacker's column and facing (place_sprite_x), where the blow lands. The low four bits are kept in $C7 for hit_score. Does nothing when all eight slots are busy.
Adds the points the record's fourth byte names (1 to 4, from hit_points, $C8C8, five decimal digits each) to the attacker's score in its panel message.
Adds five decimal digits (pointer $5F, offsets 0 to 4) to a five-digit ASCII number (pointer $7F, offsets 0 to 4), last digit first, with the carry passed on and the result kept as ASCII.
distance ($AA) = the difference between the two fighters' columns ($71, $72).

Moves both fighters on by one frame (animate_fighter), drawing them into the arena buffer in turn: fighter 1 first, then 0 on top of it, unless fighter 1 is in one of the moves at drawn_last ($BDCF: $9B the fall, $88 the headless body, $8B, $87), when fighter 0 goes first. None in the select mode; with the flag at $BB set, only fighter 0.

One frame of fighter X. First the move's sounds: when the move and frame index match an entry of move_sound_moves and move_sound_frames ($C8E1, $C8E8, seven entries), the sound move_sound_requests ($C8EF) is asked of voices 1 and 2. Then the next entry of the move's frame list (move_frames, $BCDC): a frame number goes on (the index moves past it, and next_move, $6B,x, is cleared when the list's command follows, so another move may start), or $FF and a command: 0 loops to the first frame, 1 sets the move to 1, 2 jumps to the index in the next byte, 3 starts the move in the next byte (for the turn, move $9D, also flipping the facing, shifting the column by turn_shift at $7F4A and, for fighter 1, asking for its sprite shapes to be mirrored), anything else holds the last frame. The frame's descriptor (frames, $BDD6) is then composed and drawn: clear_compose, move_fighter, compose_frame, draw_fighter.
Clears the compose buffer $05CA-$0800 (nine bytes by 63 lines).

Builds the fighter's frame in the compose buffer, nine bytes (36 multicolour pixels) wide and 63 lines tall, from the descriptor's first nine bytes: three rows of three block numbers, 0 for none. Block n is the 63 bytes at $0800 + 64 * n, three bytes a line for 21 lines, as a sprite is stored; each nonzero byte goes to its place through block_corners ($CF22) and block_offsets ($CF34). A fighter facing left ($91,x not 0) is then mirrored (mirror_compose).
Mirrors the compose buffer left to right: each of its 63 lines of nine bytes is reversed and each byte turned through mirror_table ($02AA).

Moves fighter X by the frame descriptor's bytes 9 and 10: byte 9's bit 2 moves it back by byte 10's columns and bit 3 moves it forward, both for a fighter facing right (step_flip, $7F48, swaps them for one facing left). Each step keeps the fighter inside the arena (limit_back, limit_forward) and out of the other fighter (check_overlap).
Takes the step ($AE) off fighter X's column, keeping it at 3 or more for a fighter facing right and 0 or more for one facing left.
Adds the step ($AE) to fighter X's column, keeping it at 28 or less for a fighter facing left; for one facing right only a sum of 32 or more is put back to 28.

How far the two fighters overlap after a step, as a negative number, or a positive one when they do not ($C3, the gap from fighter 0 to fighter 1 as they face). A fighter rolling forward (move $91) into the other in a jump (move $84) sets roll_past ($B2) to $84 and returns a positive number, so it rolls under. During a death the number returned is always positive. move_fighter pushes the fighter back by a negative result.

Draws the compose buffer into the arena buffer at fighter X's column: 62 of its 63 lines, eight lines to a cell row (strip_row_offsets, $CF7C), its nine bytes a line into nine cells (cell_offsets, $CF73). Each nonzero byte is drawn through mask_table: the arena's byte ANDed with the mask and ORed with the fighter's, so the background shows through the see-through pixels. The arena buffer has the bitmap's layout, 320 bytes a cell row, from $A6BD for column 0. During a death the drawing is clipped (draw_fighter_clip).
draw_fighter for a fighter being dragged off: the same drawing, but bytes for column 40 and beyond are left out.

Copies the arena strip of the bitmap, cell rows 14 to 21, columns 4 to 35 (eight runs of 256 bytes from $71A0), into the clean copy at $B0DD, which keeps the bitmap's 320 bytes a row, so it runs to $BA9C. Run when a backdrop is set up.
Copies the clean copy ($B0DD) over the arena buffer ($A6DD onwards), wiping the last frame's fighters.
Copies the arena buffer back into the bitmap's strip ($71A0 onwards), the eight cell rows of 256 bytes, showing the new frame.

When flip_request ($B7) is negative, clears its bit 7 and mirrors the 45 sprite shapes at $54C0-$5FFF (sprite pointers $53-$7F), fighter 1's coloured body pieces: in each of a shape's 21 lines the three bytes change places end for end and each goes through mirror_table ($02AA). Bit 0 of $B7 then says which way the shapes face (1: mirrored, for fighter 1 facing right). The turn asks for this when fighter 1 turns round; the end of a bout, the F1 key and the restart ask for it again to put them back.

Exchanges the 4-by-4-cell picture at cell row 9, column 13 of the bitmap ($6BA8) with the stash at $04AA, and its colour RAM ($D975) with the stash at $05AA (swap_4x4_cells): in the hall of arches, Drax in the left-hand arch. The stash holds plain light blue (fill_cell_stash: bytes $FF, all pixels in the colour RAM's colour, $0E), so the arch is left empty. Run by start_ending, and by restart_game, which puts him back.

The same for the picture at cell row 9, column 23 ($6BF8, colour RAM $D97F), Mariana in the right-hand arch, with the stashes at $052A and $05BA. Run by reach_drax when she comes down, and by restart_game after it.

Exchanges four cell rows of 32 bitmap bytes (four cells each) between (pointer $75), 320 bytes a row, and (pointer $77), 32 bytes a row; then four rows of four colour RAM bytes between (pointer $7B), 40 a row, and (pointer $79), four a row.

Exchanges the 13 sprite shapes at $FC40-$FF7F, under the KERNAL, with the first 13 of fighter 1's body pieces at $54C0-$581F (sprite pointers $53-$5F): Mariana, Drax and his star in, for the ending. Run by start_ending, and by restart_game to put them back.

Once a main-loop pass while the ending runs (scene_flag, $BB, negative): reads entry $CB of scene_records ($CD09), a pointer to a record of twelve bytes (the four records are at $CD11, $CD1D, $CD29 and $CD35), and from the record starts sprites 3 to 0 again. Byte 0 is sprite 3's picture sequence and byte 3 sprite 0's (0 switches the sprite off); bytes 4 to 7 are their X, with the ninth bit set for all four, and bytes 8 to 11 their Y, plus $A2.

Changes the backdrop: between bouts, and back to the first when a game is chosen or restarted. Fades the sound out ($E2) and waits for the fade, then with interrupts off turns the background black and the sprites off, flips backdrop ($C4, 0 or 1), wipes the fighters off the screen (clear_strip, show_strip), lifts the arena out of the bitmap (lift_arena), exchanges its screen colours with the stashed backdrop's (swap_arena_colours), colours the fighters' strip (colour_strip), brings in the stashed backdrop and stashes the old one (drop_arena), saves the clean strip (save_strip, clear_strip) and fades the sound back in ($E1).

Copies the arena of the bitmap, cell rows 7 to 22 and columns 4 to 35, into the buffer at $A6BD as one 4,096-byte block (256 bytes a cell row), clearing each byte of the bitmap behind it. It runs with $01 = $20 (all RAM) and puts $01 back.

Exchanges the buffer at $A6BD with the stashed backdrop in the RAM under the I/O chips, $D000-$DFFF (swap_stash), then copies the buffer into the bitmap's arena, cell row 22 first and up to row 7, so the stashed backdrop is drawn and the one that was on screen is stashed. Runs with $01 = $20, all RAM, and puts $01 back.

For cell row $9B, line $9A of the cell and arena column X (0 to 31): pointer $77 = the bitmap byte (bitmap_row_address, $7FCE, plus 32 for column 4, plus X times 8), pointer $75 = the buffer byte ($A6BD plus 256 for each row after row 7, plus X times 8), and Y = the line.
Exchanges 16 pages, $A6BD-$B6BC with $D000-$DFFF, a byte at a time.

Exchanges the arena's colours with the stashed backdrop's: 16 rows of 32 screen bytes from $451C (cell row 7, column 4) with $E11C, and the same rows of colour RAM from $D91C with $E51C, 40 bytes a row on screen and in the stash alike.

Places the sprites that go over each fighter's frame. For fighter 1 and then fighter 0, unless it has been dragged to column 30 or beyond, the frame's descriptor (frames, $BDD6, from the pose $6F,x) gives a count (byte 11) and four bytes for each sprite: shape, colour, Y and X offset (place_overlay). The sprites are taken from 7 downwards. The first sprite of almost every frame is one of fighter 1's coloured body pieces (shape $33 or more), which fighter 0 leaves out, so only fighter 1 wears them; the others show what rises above the strip the fighters are drawn in: the top of the head, a fist or the sword. Every sprite below the last one used is switched off unless a picture sequence is running on it (blood, the head, the goblin).

One overlay sprite for fighter $9D in sprite $A3. Its pointer is the shape byte plus $20: shapes below $33 (pointers $20-$52, $4800-$54BF) have a mirrored copy 13 shapes on for a fighter facing left (shape_offset, $7F46); fighter 1's body pieces ($53-$7F) are used as they are, since flip_sprite_shapes mirrors that whole bank. With bit 7 of the colour byte set the sprite is multicolour in that colour; with it clear it is hi-res in the skill level's colour (level_colours, $C8F6), so fighter 1 changes colour from level to level. Then the Y byte goes into the Y shadow and the X offset to place_sprite_x.

Sprite $A3's X from fighter $9D's column and an offset (at (pointer $89),Y): X = column times 8 + 24 + offset for a fighter facing right, or + 48 - offset for one facing left, so the offset is mirrored with the fighter. The ninth bit goes into the X MSB shadow ($12).

After a roll under a jump (roll_past, $B2, negative), once the fighter in the jump (move $84) has landed (pose 0), turns both fighters round (move $9D), since they now face away from each other. The turn's command ends the roll past.

When a fighter is in the headless body's move ($88) and no death is recorded yet: records it (dead, $AF = the fighter's number with bit 7) and starts three sprites at its neck, X = column times 8 plus 24 facing right or 72 facing left (death_x_offset, $CE46). Sprite 0 is the head, rolling (sequence $80 or $81 by facing, head_sequences at $CE48) and flying off in an arc that bounces three times (motion $81 or $82, head_motions at $CE50); sprite 1, at Y $CD on the floor, its shadow (sequence $83, motion $83 or $84); sprite 2, at Y $9D, blood spurting from the neck (sequence $82, standing still). Then falls into winner_move.

Gives the winner its move after a death: winner ($B6) is set to the winner's number with bit 7 (the time bonus is owed). After a decapitation (the loser in move $88) or with the fighters 2 or more columns apart, the winner's move is $93 (frames $3C, $00, $2F, $2F, $30, $31 five times, $30, $2F, $2F, and the last held); otherwise $9C, frames $1B, $1C, $46 and $00, which then goes on into $93.

Once the loser is lying on the ground (pose $59 or $14) and the goblin has not come yet ($B0 positive), sends it in: two sprites, 3 for its top half (Y $B8) and 4 for its bottom half (Y $CD), at X 39 on the left, walking (sequences $86 and $87) to the right a pixel a frame (motion $85). Sets $B0 to $FF.

Colours the snakes' squares at the top of the two pillars, cell rows 2 to 5: columns 0 to 3 with screen bytes $73 (yellow and cyan) and colour RAM $0E (light blue), columns 36 to 39 with $7D (yellow and light green) and $05 (green).

Colours the strip the fighters are drawn in, cell rows 14 to 21 and columns 4 to 35: screen bytes $C0 (medium grey and black) and colour RAM $0A (light red), the fighters' own three colours, whichever backdrop is behind them.

Clears the game's flags and states (dead, goblin, drag, roll past, walk-back, flip_request, winner, started, select, the flags at $BB and $BC, players, pause, backdrop, $CB, the interrupt's busy flag and the sequencer's at $98), sets demo ($B3) to 1 and the skill level ($BE) to 4, and fills the cell stashes (fill_cell_stash).
Fills $04AA-$05A9 with $FF and $05AA-$05C9 with $0E, the stashes that swap_cells_13 and swap_cells_23 exchange with the screen.
Sets the clock to 90 seconds ($C8) and its frame count to 50 ($C9).

Clears the sprite X and Y shadow ($02-$12) and the enable shadow ($17), switches every sprite off and clears its Y and X expansion, multicolour, priority and collision registers, and makes the border black.

Prints message A ($80 to $97) into the bitmap. The address is entry A AND $7F of message_pointers ($BABD). A message is one or more records: column, cell row, a colour byte, then characters up to a carriage return ($0D), which starts the next record, or any character the font lacks (each message ends with "$"). A to Z are glyphs 1 to 26, and the thirteen characters at font_chars ($BC77: 0 to 9, space and the two half circles, "(" and ")") have their glyph numbers at font_glyphs ($BC84). A glyph's eight bytes (glyph_address) are drawn in two colours: a pixel whose left bit is set takes the colour byte's low four bits, from colour RAM, and the rest its high four bits, from the screen.
Pointer $73 = the font at $E800 plus 8 times glyph A.

The keyboard, once a main-loop pass, through CIA 1's matrix (port A as outputs picking a row, port B read back). CTRL and V held together print message $81 (V 05 10 87 and HELLO CLAIRE) in the middle of the arena, with the interrupt's sprite work stopped (pause, $C1), for as long as V is down, then recolour the strip. F1 enters the select mode when no game, death, roll past or select is under way: skill level 0, demo off, the first backdrop, both fighters reset; each pass F1 is held then sets one player ($BD = 0; side 1 switches between one and two here) and resets the clock. F3 fades the sound out and switches sound_mode ($B8): negative plays the title tune on the three voices ($80, $81, $82) and keeps the effects out, positive the effects alone; then fades back in. F5 pauses outside the select mode: the sprite work stops, a delay of about a second (pause_delay) lets go of the key, and the game waits for F5 again; that press is not waited out, so F5 still down at the next pass pauses again. F7 starts the game from the select mode (started, $B9 = $80). Q restarts (restart_game). Port A and B are put back as inputs at the end, for the joysticks.
Waits for any fade in to finish, then fades the volume out ($E2 = $81: one step every tick of the sequencer) and waits until it is silent, then clears the sound (silence) with interrupts off.
A busy wait of 65,536 turns of a loop of 13 cycles, about 850,000 cycles: close to 0.9 seconds on a PAL machine.

The Q key, and the end of a game: switches the sprites off and stops their slots, wipes the fighters off the screen, recolours the strip, puts fighter 1's body pieces back to face left; after the ending puts Drax back in his arch and the scene shapes away (scene_flag, $BB) and Mariana back in hers (scene_flag_2, $BC); and with the second backdrop up changes back to the first. Then resets the stack and starts again at restart ($800E).

The interrupt handler, for the video chip and CIA 1. A raster interrupt runs raster_irq. Then CIA 1's interrupt control register is read, which acknowledges it, and kept in $97: timer B's interrupt runs the sound sequencer (sound_tick, $9960) and timer A's the sound effects (effects_tick, $9EDF), each with interrupts enabled again first, so a raster interrupt can break into them. A timer A interrupt that comes while sound_tick runs finds the sequencer busy ($98) and does nothing, but leaves its flags in $97, so the interrupted handler runs effects_tick as soon as sound_tick returns.
The NMI handler: returns at once, so RESTORE does nothing.

Splits the screen in two colours. At any line above $FA (the interrupt set for line $72, under the panel) it sets the next interrupt at line $FA and the background colour to the backdrop's (backdrop_colours, $7F40, dark grey for both). At line $FA it sets the next interrupt at line $72 and the background to black for the border and the panel, then, unless the last frame's work is still running (busy, $CE), does this frame's: the sprite registers, and when not paused ($C1) the sprites' motion, the goblin, the motion scripts, the picture sequences and the counters.
Moves the eight sprites by their direction bits ($027A: 1 up, 2 down, 4 left, 8 right) and speeds ($028A for Y, $0282 for X, in pixels a frame).
Sprite X's Y less its Y speed, kept at $32 or more.
Sprite X's Y plus its Y speed, kept at $E5 or less.

Sprite X's X less its X speed, with the ninth bit cleared on a borrow. A sprite that moves left of 56 (ninth bit clear) leaves the screen: its picture sequence and motion script stop and it is switched off.

Sprite X's X plus its X speed, with the ninth bit set on a carry. A sprite at 300 or more (ninth bit set and low byte $2C or more) leaves the screen: its picture sequence stops and it is switched off, and its motion script stops unless it is the goblin's walk ($85).
The goblin's work, once a frame while it is on screen ($B0 negative): reaching the head, dragging the body and reaching the body.

After a decapitation, while the head (sprite 0) is still showing: when the goblin's top half (sprite 3) is exactly 8 pixels left of the head, it kicks the head away: the head and its shadow get new motion scripts ($86, $87, kick_motions at $CE54), the head bouncing off to the right, and new picture sequences ($80 rolling, $83 the shadow, kick_sequences at $CE4C); the kick's sound, $EB, goes to all three voices when voice 1 has no sequence playing and no request.

While the goblin drags ($B1 negative): starts the drag's sound ($D4, $D5, $D6 on the three voices) whenever voice 1 has no sequence playing and no request, so it repeats; and each time the goblin's X reaches a multiple of 8, moves the loser's body a column right if it is more than 5 columns behind the goblin (goblin_column).

After a death, before the drag: when the goblin's column is the body's plus 5, at its far edge (goblin_column), stops it for 100 frames with two pictures of its own (motion scripts $88 and $89, sequences $88 and $89, at grab_motions $CE56 and grab_sequences $CE4E), after which it walks on to the right and the body follows; sets drag ($B1) to $FF and asks voice 1 for sound $E2.

$C5 = the goblin's column (the X of its top half, sprite 3, with its ninth bit, divided by 8, less 3), and compares the loser's column plus 5 with it (carry set when the body is not behind by more than that, zero when they are equal).
For each sprite whose picture sequence ($0292,x) is running (bit 7 set): switches it on in the enable shadow ($17) and steps its sequence (step_sequence).

One frame of sprite X's picture sequence (picture_sequences, $CC54). While the picture's frames ($029A,x) last it only counts them down. Then the sequence's header is read again: byte 0, the frames for each picture, and byte 1, the colour in its low four bits, multicolour in bit 7, double width in bit 6 and double height in bit 5. The entry at the read index ($02A2,x, from 2) is the next picture (pointer = entry + $20), or $FF and a command: 0 starts again at the first picture, 1 ends the sequence and switches the sprite off, 2 jumps to the entry in the next byte, and anything else starts the sequence in the next byte.
For each sprite whose motion script ($025A,x) is running (bit 7 set) steps it (step_motion); the others get no direction, so sprite_motion leaves them still.

One frame of sprite X's motion script (motion_script_table, $CD4F). Steps are four bytes: direction bits, speeds (X in the high four bits, Y in the low four), frames, command. While a step's frames ($0262,x) last it only counts them down. At the end of a step with command 0 the next step is read (offset $026A,x, four bytes on); command 1 starts the motion script and picture sequence in the next two bytes, 2 starts the motion script in the next byte at once, 3 jumps to the step numbered in the next byte, 4 stops the sprite and switches it off, and any other value asks voice 1 for the sound in the next byte and goes on.
Clears sprite X's motion counters: frames, command and offset ($0262, $0272, $026A). Returns A = 0.

Copies the sprite shadow into the video chip: X and Y and the X ninth bits ($02-$12 to $D000-$D010), the colours ($29-$30 to $D027-$D02E), the pointers ($4A-$51 into $47F8-$47FF, after the screen at $4400) and the enable bits ($17 to $D015).

The counters the interrupt keeps, once a frame: both idle counters ($95, $96) down to 0; the clock, outside a walk-on, a walk-back or a death and until it reaches 0, one second ($C8) each 50 frames ($C9); and wait_count ($CA) down to 0.

The sequencer, on each interrupt of CIA 1's timer B: 47.3 times a second at the latch restart sets ($5161), and at the rate a tune's tempo command picks (35.9 a second for tempo 10, which the title tune uses). Returns at once if a tick is already running (busy, $98). For voices 3, 2 and 1 in turn: a waiting request ($DD-$DF) starts its sequence (start_request); then, for a voice with a sequence playing ($0251,x negative) whose note has run its time (duration $0218, two bytes, at 0), reads the sequence on from its offset ($021E): commands are carried out (do_command) until a note (a byte below $C0, play_note) or a command that ends the tick's reading ($E7 negative). Then counts the notes' time down (count_durations), steps a fade (fade_step) and puts the volume ($E0) into the volume register's shadow ($49).

Starts note A (the note number times 2) on the voice: the frequency from note_freqs ($9F00 plus 2 times A, two bytes) into the voice's shadow registers; the instrument's effect delay ($0248) and effect flags ($0236) into the running ones ($023C, $0239); the first of its three effect pairs, step and count, from $0200 and $0209 (three each a voice), with the pair index and steps done at 0; the duration ($0218) set to the note length ($0212); the filter sweep restarted from its first phase and its starting cutoff (set_cutoff); the instrument's pulse width ($022A) into the shadow; and the gate switched on (and the test bit off). The read offset moves past the note.

Carries out a command byte at the read pointer ($D3). $C0 to $CF set the note length ($0212) to length_ticks entry n ($A080: 3, 6, 9, 12, 18, 24, 36, 48, 72, 96, 144, 4, 8, 16, 576 and 768 ticks). $F0 to $F9 are found in command_bytes ($A0C8) and jumped to through command_handlers ($A0D2), with Y on the byte after the command. Any other byte returns without moving the offset, so the reading would take it again for ever; no sequence holds one.
$F0: waits a note length with no new note, the gate left as it is, and ends the tick's reading.
$F1: switches the gate off and puts the read offset back to the start of the sequence.
$F2: ends the voice's sequence ($0251,x = 0), its effects and the filter sweep, and the tick's reading. Most of the sound effects end with it.

$F3 n: instrument n, twelve bytes at instruments ($A3C9 + 12 n): attack and decay, sustain and release, the waveform (high four bits) and the pulse width's high four bits, inverted (low four), the pulse width's low byte, inverted; the delay between effect steps; the effect flags (bit 7 on, bit 6 steps in pitch, bit 5 steps in pulse width, bit 4 a slide in frequency, bit 3 repeat the pairs, bit 2 ring modulation on triangle, bit 1 sync); and three pairs of a step and a count. The envelope and the waveform go into the voice's shadow registers straight away, the waveform with the gate off.
$F4 a b: sets the note length to the sum of two lengths, length_ticks entries a and b (their low four bits).
$F5 n: the voice goes on with sequence $80 + n from its start, with the filter taken off it. The tunes repeat this way.
$F6 n: sets CIA 1's timer B, the sequencer's tick, to tempo_latches entry n ($A0A0).
$F7 n: plays sequence $80 + n from its start and comes back after it: the sequence and the offset after the command are kept ($0254, $0224) for $F8. One level deep.
$F8: goes back to the sequence and offset that $F7 kept.

$F9 n: filter setting n, at filter_settings ($A0E6, eleven bytes each): the delay between sweep steps ($EB), the starting cutoff ($D6 and $D5), the resonance and voice routing with this voice added ($48), the filter mode with voice 3 left on ($49, keeping the volume), and three phases of a step (times 8) and a count of steps.
Adds A to voice $E5's read offset ($021E, two bytes).
Counts each voice's note time ($0218) down by one a tick; when it reaches 0 the gate goes off, so each note has its release before the next. Also counts the fade's timer ($E3) down.

On each tick of timer A, for each voice with effects on ($0239 bit 7) and its delay ($023C) run out: steps the current pair (pitch_step, pulse_step, slide_step, as the flags say), counts the step and sets the delay again ($0248). When the pair's steps are done it takes the next of the three pairs, after the third going back to the first if the flags' bit 3 is set or switching the effects off. A pair with a count of 0 is passed over.

With flag bit 6: moves the voice's pitch ($024E, an index into note_freqs) by the pair's step, in quarter tones (two to a semitone), and sets the frequency from the table. Past the top of the table's 192 entries it wraps round to the bottom (190 plus 4 gives 2); below the bottom it lands one entry higher than a wrap would (sbc #$3F with the carry set: 2 less 4 gives 191, and 0 less 1 gives 192, the word after the table).
With flag bit 5: adds the pair's step times 16 to the voice's pulse width, kept to twelve bits.
With flag bit 4: adds the pair's step straight to the voice's frequency, upwards, or downwards when bit 7 of the pair's count is set (the step is then added less 256).

On each tick of timer A, when a filter setting with a sweep is on ($EB not 0) and its delay ($E9) has run out: moves the cutoff by the current phase's step (filter_step) and counts the step, setting the delay again; after the phase's count it takes the next of the three phases, and after the third starts again from the first unless the second phase's step ($0232) is 0, when the sweep stops where it is.
Adds the phase's step ($0230 + 2 x phase) to the cutoff ($DB, $DC), kept to eleven bits, then sets it (set_cutoff).
Splits the eleven-bit cutoff ($DB, $DC) into the filter's two registers' shadows: the low three bits into $46 ($D415) and the high eight into $47 ($D416).

Starts the request in $DD,x on voice X. A sound effect (any request from $83 on) is dropped while the title tune plays (sound_mode, $B8, negative); the tune's own three ($80 to $82) are always taken. The voice's sequence becomes the request, its effects, time and offset are cleared, its gate goes off, the filter is taken off it and the filter sweep stops.

When the fade's timer ($E3) has run out: a fade in ($E1 negative) raises the volume ($E0) by one, ending at 15; a fade out ($E2 negative) lowers it by one, ending at 0. The timer is set again from the fade's low seven bits, the ticks between steps.
Clears the shadow of the SID's 25 registers and the registers themselves, the driver's variables at $0200-$0259 and its zero page, $CF-$EE: the requests, the volume and the fades included.
Copies the shadow ($31-$49) into the SID's registers, $D400-$D418.

On each interrupt of CIA 1's timer A, 98.5 times a second (latch $2710), unless the sequencer is running: counts each voice's effect delay ($023C) and the filter sweep's delay ($E9) down, runs the voices' effects (voice_effects) and the sweep (filter_sweep), and writes the shadow into the SID (write_sid). Apart from silence, nothing else writes the SID's registers.

The SID frequencies of 192 pitches a quarter tone apart, two bytes each, from 268 up to 65,535. A note n in a sequence plays entry 2n, a semitone a step; the effects step through the quarter tones between. Entry 96, note 48, is 4,291: 261.6 Hz at an NTSC machine's clock (middle C), 252.0 Hz at a PAL machine's, 65 cents flat.
Entries 128 to 191 of note_freqs, which starts at $9F00: the top 64 pitches, from the memory-map edge at $A000.
Note lengths in sequencer ticks, for the commands $C0-$CF: 3, 6, 9, 12, 18, 24, 36, 48, 72, 96, 144, 4, 8, 16, 576 and 768.

Seventeen latches for CIA 1's timer B, the sequencer's tick, chosen by the $F6 command: from $F424 (15.8 ticks a second on a PAL machine) down to $30D4 (78.8). Tempo 10, $6B50, is 35.9 ticks a second.
Each voice's first register in the SID and its shadow: 0, 7 and 14.
Each voice's first entry in the effect-pair tables at $0200 and $0209: 0, 3 and 6.
The sequence commands do_command looks up: $F0 to $F9.
The routine for each command in command_bytes: wait, restart, end, instrument, long note, go to, tempo, call, return, filter.
Pointers to the sixteen filter settings the $F9 command picks.
Filter setting 0: cutoff 2047 of 2,047, resonance 1, routing bits $07 plus the voice that asks, high-pass, no sweep.
